name: stat
title: Stat
description: Stat. Best for: One headline number and how it has moved. Up to four in a row.

files.content:
import type { HTMLAttributes, Ref } from 'react' import { ArrowDownRight, ArrowUpRight } from 'lucide-react' import { cn } from '../../../lib/cn' export type StatDelta = { /** Already formatted, e.g. "12%". */ value: string direction: 'up' | 'down' /** Whether this movement is good. Independent of direction: fewer failed syncs is down AND good. */ sentiment: 'positive' | 'negative' | 'neutral' /** What it is compared with, e.g. "last week". Spoken and shown. */ period: string } export type StatProps = HTMLAttributes & { label: string /** Integers are padded; anything else (e.g. "4.2k") is shown as given. */ value: number | string unit?: string /** Pad an integer value to this many digits with dimmed, aria-hidden zeros. */ padTo?: number delta?: StatDelta ref?: Ref } /** Direction is shown as a shape (an arrow); sentiment is coloured -- on the arrow only -- and * spoken. They are independent props because the two do not always agree: fewer failed syncs is * a `down` delta with a `positive` sentiment. The `sr-only` sentence below states direction, * amount, period AND sentiment together, so a screen-reader user gets the full picture. **For a * sighted user, sentiment currently rests on the arrow's colour alone** -- direction has the * arrow's shape, but nothing shape- or word-codes sentiment independent of hue. Sentiment stays * on the arrow's colour only (accepted by Victor, 2026-09-24); see `BUILD-LOG.md`'s Stat entry * for the two alternatives considered (a visible word, or a second glyph). * * The tone colour paints ONLY the arrow glyph, a graphic. `accent.ok.text` / `accent.hostile.text` * are gated at 4.5:1 on `surface.base` by contrast-pairs.mjs's "accent.ok.text on surface.base" * and "accent.hostile.text on surface.base" rows, and at 3:1 (SC 1.4.11's graphic floor) on * `surface.raised` by "alert icon and border (accent..text) on surface.raised (over * surface.base)" -- reused rather than duplicated. Neutral's `text.secondary` icon clears both * floors via that token's own 4.5:1 body-text rows ("text.secondary on surface.base" and "alert * body and ghost dismiss (text.secondary) on surface.raised"). * * The delta's amount and period text is `text.secondary`, NOT the tone colour: the arrow already * carries the sentiment, and a tone colour on the amount would make the least important part of * the delta the loudest. `text.secondary` keeps the amount and the "vs {period}" qualifier one * quiet colour, gated at 4.5:1 on both surfaces by the same two rows named above. */ const SENTIMENT = { positive: { className: 'text-[var(--color-accent-ok-text)]', words: 'an improvement' }, negative: { className: 'text-[var(--color-accent-hostile-text)]', words: 'a decline' }, neutral: { className: 'text-[var(--color-text-secondary)]', words: 'neither better nor worse' }, } as const /** * One number that matters, and how it has moved. The numerals-as-heroes motif as a component. * * Semantics are a `dl` pair turned inside out: `label` is a `dt`, `value` a `dd`, so a screen * reader hears "Kits dispatched, 18" -- the natural reading order, and also the natural visual * one (the label sits above, small and quiet; the value below, at display size). * * The pad follows Progress and the Overview's own numeral treatment exactly: dimmed zeros in * `--color-numeral-pad`, `aria-hidden`, the significant digits in `text.primary`. It is opt-in * (`padTo`) because a pad is only honest when the field width is real -- an unbounded value (the * Slider readout's reason for having none) would be inventing digits. * * The label reads `text.secondary`, matching Progress's own small mono readout label -- not * `text.label`, which an earlier draft of this component used. `text.label` is dimmed on purpose for * reading as a heading over a list rather than another item in it (the sidebar's group names), * and measures only 4.00:1 on `surface.raised` in dark theme, below the 4.5:1 body-text floor. * Stat has no surface of its own -- it inherits whatever it is dropped onto, and a Stat inside a * Panel or a Card (both `surface.raised`) is exactly as valid a use as one loose on the page * (`surface.base`, where `text.label` does pass). `text.secondary` is already gated on both * surfaces and clears AA with real headroom in both themes, so it works everywhere a Stat can * legitimately be placed. Stat's own docs Examples happen to render inside a Panel, which is * how this surfaced. */ export function Stat({ label, value, unit, padTo, delta, className, ref, ...rest }: StatProps) { const digits = String(value) const pad = typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 && padTo ? '0'.repeat(Math.max(0, padTo - digits.length)) : '' const Arrow = delta?.direction === 'down' ? ArrowDownRight : ArrowUpRight return (
{label}
{pad ? ( {pad} ) : null} {digits} {unit ? ( {unit} ) : null}
{delta ? (

{delta.value} vs {delta.period} {delta.direction} {delta.value} from {delta.period}, {SENTIMENT[delta.sentiment].words}

) : null}
) }
